{{Short description|1=Researcher, Ph.D. Radboud Universiteit Nijmegen 2009, ORCID ID = 0000–0002-8273-6059}}
'''Cezary Kaliszyk''' (born 1981) is a Polish computer scientist and professor of theoretical computer science at the [[University of Melbourne]]. His research focuses on [[automated reasoning]], formal mathematics, [[proof assistant]]s, and the application of artificial intelligence and machine learning to mathematical reasoning.

== Education ==
Kaliszyk studied computer science and mathematics at the [[University of Warsaw]]. He received a PhD in computer science from [[Radboud University Nijmegen]] in 2009<ref>{{cite web
 |title=PhD Students
 |publisher=Radboud University
 |url=https://www.cs.ru.nl/~herman/phdstudents.html
 |access-date=9 September 2026
}}</ref> and completed his habilitation in computer science at the [[University of Innsbruck]] in 2016.<ref>{{cite web
|title=Abgeschlossene Habilitationsverfahren Standort Technik
|publisher=University of Innsbruck
|language=de
|url=https://www.uibk.ac.at/de/fakultaeten-servicestelle/standorte/technikerstrasse/abgeschlossene-habilitationsverfahren-standort-technik/
|access-date=9 September 2026
}}</ref>

== Career ==

Kaliszyk held postdoctoral positions at the [[Technical University of Munich]] and the [[University of Tsukuba]] before joining the University of Innsbruck in 2012. In 2024, he joined the University of Melbourne as a professor of theoretical computer science.

In 2016, Kaliszyk received a [[European Research Council]] Starting Grant for the SMART project (''Strong Modular proof Assistance: Reasoning across Theories'').<ref>{{cite web |title=Informatiker erhält ERC-Preis |publisher=University of Innsbruck |date=6 October 2016 |language=de |url=https://www.uibk.ac.at/de/newsroom/2016/informatiker-erhaelt-erc-preis/ |access-date=8 September 2026}}</ref> The project investigated automated proof assistance and methods for combining automated reasoning with machine learning.<ref>{{cite web |title=CORDIS: Strong Modular proof Assistance: Reasoning across Theories (SMART) |publisher=European Commission |url=https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/714034 |access-date=8 September 2026}}</ref> Kaliszyk was involved in [[EuroProofNet]], the European Research Network on Formal Proofs, and led its working group on machine learning in proofs.<ref>{{cite web |title=What Can Formal Systems Do For Mathematics? A Discussion Through the Lens of Proof Assistants: Some Recent Advances |publisher=University of Hamburg |url=https://www.math.uni-hamburg.de/spag/ml/DVMLG/DVMLG60/dvmlg60_book.pdf |access-date=8 September 2026}}</ref> In 2025, Kaliszyk received an AI for Math grant from Renaissance Philanthropy for research on artificial intelligence systems for mathematical and symbolic reasoning.<ref>{{cite web |title=University researcher awarded $1.5m to advance AI in mathematics |publisher=University of Melbourne |url=https://about.unimelb.edu.au/news-resources/awards-and-achievements/research-grants-funding/University-researcher-awarded-%241.5m-to-advance-AI-in-mathematics |access-date=8 September 2026}}</ref>
